**Bernabéu** ([Spanish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_language "Spanish language"): _El Bernabéu_[[βeɾnaˈβew]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Spanish "Help:IPA/Spanish") [](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/7/71/ES-pe_-_Estadio_Santiago_Bernab%C3%A9u.ogg/ES-pe_-_Estadio_Santiago_Bernab%C3%A9u.ogg.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:ES-pe_-_Estadio_Santiago_Bernab%C3%A9u.ogg "File:ES-pe - Estadio Santiago Bernabéu.ogg")**Santiago Bernabéu Stadium** , is a [retractable roof](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retractable_roof "Retractable roof") [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") stadium in the [district of Chamartín](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chamart%C3%ADn_\(Madrid\) "Chamartín \(Madrid\)"), [Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madrid "Madrid"), Spain. With a seating capacity of 83,186[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-:2-7) following its extensive renovation completed in late 2024, the stadium has the second-largest seating capacity for a football stadium in Spain, behind [Camp Nou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camp_Nou "Camp Nou") in Barcelona. It has been the home stadium of [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_C.F. "Real Madrid C.F.") since its completion in 1947.
Named after former Real Madrid player and [president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Real_Madrid_CF_presidents "List of Real Madrid CF presidents") [Santiago Bernabéu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santiago_Bernab%C3%A9u "Santiago Bernabéu") (1895–1978), the stadium is one of the world's most famous football venues. It has hosted the final of the [European Cup/UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League") on four occasions: in [1957](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1957_European_Cup_Final "1957 European Cup Final"), [1969](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1969_European_Cup_Final "1969 European Cup Final"), [1980](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_European_Cup_Final "1980 European Cup Final") and [2010](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_UEFA_Champions_League_Final "2010 UEFA Champions League Final").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-8) The stadium also hosted the second leg of the [2018 Copa Libertadores Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Copa_Libertadores_Finals "2018 Copa Libertadores Finals"), making Santiago Bernabéu the only stadium to host finals of both competitions.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-9) The final matches for the [1964 European Nations' Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1964_European_Nations'_Cup "1964 European Nations' Cup") and the [1982 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_FIFA_World_Cup "1982 FIFA World Cup") were also held at the Bernabéu, making it the first stadium in Europe to host both a [UEFA Euro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_European_Championship "UEFA European Championship") [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1964_European_Nations'_Cup_final "1964 European Nations' Cup final") and a [FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup "FIFA World Cup") [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_FIFA_World_Cup_final "1982 FIFA World Cup final").
## History
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]
### Origins and construction
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Origins and construction")]
In the early 1940s, the old [Campo de Chamartín](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estadio_Chamart%C3%ADn "Estadio Chamartín") had become too small for the growing population of Madrid and the increasing popularity of football. Despite successive renovations that had expanded its capacity to 25,000 seats, the stadium was still insufficient for the club's needs. Faced with this situation, in the spring of 1943, President [Antonio Santos Peralba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Santos_Peralba "Antonio Santos Peralba") expressed the need to build a new stadium with an initial capacity of 40,000 spectators,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-AScien-10) although the club's financial difficulties raised uncertainties about its realization.
With the arrival of [Santiago Bernabéu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santiago_Bernab%C3%A9u_\(footballer\) "Santiago Bernabéu \(footballer\)") to the presidency in September 1943, the plan for the new stadium gained decisive and much more ambitious momentum. In his first meeting with the board of directors, Bernabéu declared: "_Gentlemen, we need a bigger field and we are going to build it_ ".[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-11) Bernabéu's vision was to build an even larger stadium than the one proposed by Peralba, with a capacity close to 75,000 spectators. Bernabéu firmly believed that a larger stadium would allow the club to raise more money, which in turn would enable the club to grow, sign better players, and attract more fans, creating a virtuous cycle that would benefit the team in the long run.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-12) On 1 November 1943, the board of directors visited the land adjacent to the Campo de Chamartín, located in the extension of the [Paseo de la Castellana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paseo_de_la_Castellana "Paseo de la Castellana"), to analyze its possible expansion. These lands belonged to the "Villa Ulpiana" estate and another known as "Entrecanales", owned by the Maqueda and Chávarri families. Shortly thereafter, negotiations began to acquire them for a total cost of 3,000,000 pesetas.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-AScien-10)
On 22 June 1944, the land acquisitions were formalized before a notary: 256,667 square feet for 2,000,000 pesetas from the Ruiz del Villar family and 93,877 square feet for 1,001,069 pesetas from the Maqueda and Chávarri families. Additionally, the necessary expropriations for the urbanization of the area, including the future streets Concha Espina and Plaza de los Sagrados Corazones, cost 1,000,000 pesetas.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-AScien-10)
To choose the design for the new stadium, a Competition of Ideas and Sketches was organized, in which renowned architects participated. The architects [Pedro Muguruza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pedro_Muguruza "Pedro Muguruza") and Javier Barroso, former goalkeepers of [Athletic de Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Club_Atl%C3%A9tico_de_Madrid "Club Atlético de Madrid") and friends of Bernabéu, were part of the jury along with board members Fernando de Cárcer Disdier, first vice president, and Pedro Méndez Cuesta, board member responsible for the field and an architect by profession.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-13) In September 1944, after evaluating the seven submitted projects, the jury awarded the first prize to the design of Manuel Muñoz Monasterio and Luis Alemany Soler. The award-winning works were exhibited at the [Círculo de Bellas Artes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%ADrculo_de_Bellas_Artes "Círculo de Bellas Artes"), where they sparked great interest and debate among fans.
On 27 October 1944, the land was blessed, and construction was symbolically initiated with a groundbreaking strike by Santiago Bernabéu.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-RV-14)
The financing of the construction presented significant challenges due to the distrust of members and banking entities. Despite the skepticism of many people, including some members and supporters, regarding the project's feasibility, Bernabéu remained steadfast in his purpose. In a context where banks did not consider football a safe investment and where official support from sports organizations was not obtainable, Bernabéu delegated to treasurer Luis Corrales Ferras[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-AScien-10) the task of designing an innovative financing plan. This plan involved the issuance of bonds with mortgage guarantees on the club's properties.
The next step was crucial:[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-AScien-10) Bernabéu presented this plan to Rafael Salgado, president of Banco Mercantil e Industrial and a Real Madrid supporter. Thanks to Bernabéu's passionate and detailed explanation, Salgado agreed to finance the project, convinced of the viability and potential of the new stadium. This decision was crucial for the project's realization, and in recognition of his support, one of the streets adjacent to the stadium bears his name.
The financing plan was structured into three staggered bond issues:[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-AScien-10)
  * **First issue** of 20,000 bonds for a total of 10,000,000 pesetas on 9 November 1944.
  * **Second issue** of 30,000 bonds for 15,000,000 pesetas on 18 March 1946.
  * **Third issue** of 10,000 bonds totaling 5,000,000 pesetas on 8 October 1947.


All the issues were covered on the day they were released to the Stock Market, thanks to the enthusiasm and confidence of the members, even the most modest ones. The plan was a complete success and allowed for staggered financing adjusted to the construction needs.
The construction was awarded to the company Huarte y Compañía, S.A.,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-AScien-10)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-15) beginning in June 1945 under the direction of architects Alemany and Muñoz Monasterio and with the collaboration of civil engineer Carlos Fernández Casado.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-16) Over 30 months, the works faced numerous obstacles, from the shortage of basic materials in post-war Spain to technical difficulties due to a nearby railway link popularly known as the "tunnel of laughter". However, the project progressed with enthusiasm and dedication.
The construction of the new field took place on the grounds of the old field and on the lands of Villa Ulpiana,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-17) which could have disrupted the club's life. However, this only happened from 1946 when Real Madrid was forced to play home games at the [Stadium Metropolitano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estadio_Metropolitano_de_Madrid "Estadio Metropolitano de Madrid") during the [1946–47 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1946%E2%80%9347_La_Liga "1946–47 La Liga") and in five matches of the [1947–48 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1947%E2%80%9348_La_Liga "1947–48 La Liga").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-18) Despite these inconveniences, Real Madrid maintained its sports activities while the new stadium took shape over part of the old site and on the adjacent lands.
This is how Fernando de Cárcer Disdier, the club's first vice president, summarized the development of the construction in 1947:[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-AScien-10)
> _We encountered numerous difficulties in transporting materials. Keep in mind that we used 18,000 m 2 of gravel, 24,000 m2 of sand, 2,000,000 bricks, 900 m2 of wood, and moved about 150,000 m3 of earth. For this, we had to load 82,000 trucks of 4 tons each… On average, 150 workers worked per day, so we had to pay about 315,000 workdays. For the services and sanitation network, we installed 4.5 kilometers of stoneware, iron, and lead pipes, with 90 porcelain sinks, 125 toilets, 365 urinals, and 46 showers. There is enough space to install offices, restaurants, warehouses, and other services, but for now, we have limited ourselves to the essentials for football: 4 dressing rooms for players with their corresponding showers, a swimming pool, a massage room, and a first aid kit. An infirmary with 6 beds, a treatment room, and an emergency operating room. A dressing room for the referee with all its services. A wardrobe room with a clothing repair workshop and iron. A shoemaker, laundry, and a large gymnasium. A telephone exchange and a radio amplification center… Additionally, a room for detainees has been built, thus avoiding the need for law enforcement to be distracted by escorting them. Regarding the costs, around 16,000,000 pesetas were budgeted, but this has increased due to perfectly justified reasons, such as the nature of the terrain, the rise in material prices over these 30 months, more than 25% in some cases, and the new labor regulations in the construction industry that required safety measures not contemplated in the project. Currently (in 1947), if we were to start the construction of the stadium, its cost would rise to 45,000,000 pesetas. The amortization is planned to be completed in 20 years with our own resources, and without having started using the new field, we have already begun to amortize. This is a great success for Real Madrid and the people of Madrid_.
— Fernando de Cárcer Disdier
The total cost of the works, in round numbers, was broken down into the following items:[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-AScien-10)
  1. **Land**. Acquisitions, capital gains, real rights, stamps, writing expenses, cancellation of commitments, and lifting of the mortgage on the old Chamartín: 4,500,000 pesetas.
  2. **Loans**. Costs of the same: 2,000,000 pesetas.
  3. **Works**. Material execution of the stadium: 28,000,000 pesetas. Execution of the office: 1,500,000 pesetas.
  4. **Fees**. Architects, quantity surveyors, and awards from the Ideas and Sketches Competition: 1,300,000 pesetas.
  5. **Compensation for Expropriations** of land carried out by the City Council: 1,000,000 pesetas.


**Total disbursed** : 38,300,000 pesetas (230,183 euros).
### Opening
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Opening")]
The stadium was inaugurated on 14 December 1947 with a match between Real Madrid and the [Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portugal "Portugal") side [Os Belenenses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C.F._Os_Belenenses "C.F. Os Belenenses").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-19) After the preliminaries, at 15:30, referee [Pedro Escartín](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pedro_Escart%C3%ADn "Pedro Escartín") from the Madrid school started the match. Real Madrid striker [Sabino Barinaga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabino_Barinaga "Sabino Barinaga") scored the first goal in the 15th minute with a header. At the end of the match, Barinaga received a recognition pennant. Afterward, players and managers of both teams celebrated with a dinner. The first official match took place on 28 December 1947 on matchday 12 of La Liga against [Athletic Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletic_Bilbao "Athletic Bilbao"), which had been postponed due to the inauguration of the stadium. The match was refereed by José Fombona Fernández from the Asturian school and ended with a 5–1 victory for _Los Blancos_. The first goal was scored in the 4th minute by Madrid midfielder [Chus Alonso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chus_Alonso "Chus Alonso") after receiving a pass from Barinaga.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-20)
The stadium's official name at the time was _Estadio Real Madrid Club de Fútbol_ _Nuevo Estadio Chamartín_ English: New Chamartín Stadium _Chamartín_
### 1950s
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 1950s")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/df/Estadio_Bernabeu._Madrid_%2812117582503%29.jpg/330px-Estadio_Bernabeu._Madrid_%2812117582503%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Estadio_Bernabeu._Madrid_\(12117582503\).jpg)The stadium in 1955
The first major renovation occurred in 1955. On 19 June of that year, the stadium expanded to accommodate 125,000 spectators. Thus, the Madrid coliseum became the biggest stadium of all the participants of the newly established [European Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League").
On 4 January 1955, after the General Assembly of Members Compromisaros, it was decided that the stadium adopt its present name in honour of club president Santiago Bernabéu.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-21)
In March 1957, [floodlights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Floodlight "Floodlight") were installed to allow nighttime games. On 18 May of the same year, the new floodlights were officially inaugurated in a game against Brazilian club [Sport Recife](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sport_Club_do_Recife "Sport Club do Recife"), which Real Madrid won 5–3.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-22)
### 1960s and 1970s
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 1960s and 1970s")]
In 1965, the transfer of all the club's offices to the stadium was completed, which previously had been moved between multiple venues in the capital.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-23)
On 14 December 1972, coinciding with the 25th anniversary of the Santiago Bernabéu's inauguration, the first electronic scoreboard was installed inside the stadium and later utilized for the first time in a friendly match against the same rival that Madrid faced in 1947, the Portuguese Belenenses. The match ended with a 2–1 Real victory. Days before the scoreboard had already been used for the farewell ceremony of the Madrid legend [Paco Gento](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paco_Gento "Paco Gento").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-24)
### 1980s
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 1980s")]
The next big changes did not occur until the hosting of the [1982 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_FIFA_World_Cup "1982 FIFA World Cup") in Spain. The stadium had to adapt to the changing times and with this, architects Rafael Luis Alemany and Manuel Salinas were hired for the stadium's renovation project. The brothers were sons of Luis Alemany Soler, who carried out the original construction project next to Muñoz Monasterio. The work lasted 16 months and had a cost of 704 million [pesetas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_peseta "Spanish peseta") (US $4.7 million), of which 530 million was paid by the City of Madrid.
The improvements included a number of points. First, [FIFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA "FIFA") forced two-thirds of the seating area to be covered. For this reason, Real Madrid installed a roof covering the perimeter of the first and second tiers of seating, except the east side. The stadium's capacity was reduced from 120,000 to 90,000 spectators, starting downsizing in 1978. 24,550 of which were covered by the new roof. The project also involved remodeling the façade, the installation of new electronic signs in the north and south ends, as well as the renovation of the press areas, lockers rooms, access, and ancillary areas.
The stadium hosted four matches in the World Cup: three second-round Group Two matches ([West Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Germany_national_football_team "West Germany national football team") vs. [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/England_national_football_team "England national football team"), West Germany vs. [Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain_men's_national_football_team "Spain men's national football team"), and Spain vs. England) and the prestigious [final match](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_FIFA_World_Cup_Final "1982 FIFA World Cup Final") (Italy vs. West Germany). The final between Italy and Germany was played in front of a sold out stadium of 90,000 people.
### 1990s
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 1990s")]
Following a series of spectator fatalities in the 1980s (most notably the [Heysel Stadium in Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heysel_Stadium_disaster "Heysel Stadium disaster") and the [Hillsborough Stadium in England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillsborough_disaster "Hillsborough disaster")), English authorities released the [Taylor Report](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Report "Taylor Report") on how to improve football spectator safety in English venues. [UEFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA "UEFA") followed suit across Europe. The stadium was forced to create separate shortcuts to different stadium sections and seats for all spectators.
In 1992, the board of [Ramón Mendoza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram%C3%B3n_Mendoza "Ramón Mendoza") awarded an expansion and renovation project to Gines Navarro Construcciones, S.A. The work started on 7 February 1992 and concluded on 7 May 1994 with a final cost of more than 5 billion pesetas, substantially raising the debt of the club, which no longer had any institutional support. The work concluded with the creation of an amphitheater on the west side and in the foundations, as well as the opening of the new commercial center, "La esquina del Bernabéu". In total, 20,200 upgraded seats were installed, with each seat having a tilt of 87 degrees, ensuring a perfect view and proximity to the pitch. In addition, four entrance towers were erected on the outside, each with two staircases and a central spiral ramp, so the spectators could access the new tier and exit more quickly.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-:0-25)
With the new structure, the height of the stadium was increased from 22 m to 45 m. This caused problems during the winter, leaving two-thirds of the field of play in the shade. This lack of sunlight led to grass deterioration on the pitch. For this reason, a polypropylene pipe network was installed at a 20 cm depth under the pitch. At over 30 km long the pipe system circulates hot water, keeping the turf from freezing in cold temperatures.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-:0-25)
Also, due to the height of the stand, it was necessary to improve and increase the lighting capability. A [retractable protective roof](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retractable_roof "Retractable roof") was also installed to protect the fans from the elements. After the renovation, the stadium's capacity was 106,000 spectators.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-:0-25)
In 1997, with [Lorenzo Sanz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lorenzo_Sanz "Lorenzo Sanz") as president, UEFA required the Santiago Bernabéu to adopt an all-seating arrangement, bringing its capacity down from 106,000 to 74,328 spectators.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-:0-25)
On 20 May 1999, the Tour Bernabéu opened, along with the club museum.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-26) The Bernabéu Tour allows visitors to "experience the stadium from the perspective of Real Madrid players and coaches", offering an inside look into the world of the popular Spanish team.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-27)
### 2000s
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 2000s")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/35/Bernabeu_en_un_Madrid-Atleti.JPG/330px-Bernabeu_en_un_Madrid-Atleti.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bernabeu_en_un_Madrid-Atleti.JPG)View of the stadium during the [Madrid derby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madrid_derby "Madrid derby") in the [2006–07 La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006%E2%80%9307_La_Liga "2006–07 La Liga") [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/19/2010_Champions_League_Final_opening_ceremony.jpg/330px-2010_Champions_League_Final_opening_ceremony.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2010_Champions_League_Final_opening_ceremony.jpg)[2010 UEFA Champions League final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2010 UEFA Champions League final") opening ceremony
As the club kept growing in all regards, thoughts for further changes to the stadium appeared.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-28) When [Florentino Pérez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florentino_P%C3%A9rez "Florentino Pérez") became the president of the club, he launched a "_Master Plan_ " with one goal: to improve the comfort of the Santiago Bernabéu and the quality of its facilities, and maximise revenue for the stadium.
Pérez invested [€](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euro "Euro")127 million in five years (2001–2006) by adding an expansion to the east side of the stadium, as well as adding a new façade on Father Damien street, new boxes and VIP areas, new dressing rooms, a new stage in honour of the east side, a new press area (also located on the east side), a new audio system, new bars, integration of heating in the stands, panoramic lifts, new restaurants, escalators in the tower access, and implementation of the multipurpose building in Father Damien street. Following the enlargement of the lateral east side and the creation of new galleries, the capacity of the Santiago Bernabéu was expanded to 80,354, all seated.
After these renovations, on 14 November 2007, one month before the 60th anniversary of the stadium's opening, UEFA awarded the Santiago Bernabéu the category of [Elite Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_stadium_categories "UEFA stadium categories") and designated it as the venue for the [2010 UEFA Champions League final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2010 UEFA Champions League final").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-29)
### 2010s and 2020s
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: 2010s and 2020s")]
In the summer of 2011, expansion work was carried out in the first amphitheater, adding an additional row to the overhang of the grandstand, which increased the capacity by 900 seats, reaching a total capacity of 81,044 spectators.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-30) In December 2018, the Santiago Bernabéu Stadium was selected as the venue for the second leg of the Copa Libertadores de América final, becoming the first stadium in the world to host the final of four of the five most important tournaments in the world: the [FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup "FIFA World Cup"), the [UEFA European Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_European_Championship "UEFA European Championship"), the [Copa América](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Am%C3%A9rica "Copa América"), the [Copa Libertadores de América](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Libertadores_de_Am%C3%A9rica "Copa Libertadores de América"), and the [UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-32)
#### Renovation (2019–2024)
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Renovation \(2019–2024\)")]
After investing a total of 256 million euros since 2000,[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-33) the board of directors, led by [Florentino Pérez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florentino_P%C3%A9rez "Florentino Pérez"), decided to take advantage of the stadium's prime location to launch an ambitious renovation project with a dual objective: to transform the Santiago Bernabéu into a global icon of sport architecture[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] and to make it one of the club's main sources of direct revenue, allowing it to continue competing economically with clubs owned by large private capital in the future.
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/09/Estadio_Santiago_Bernab%C3%A9u_38.jpg/330px-Estadio_Santiago_Bernab%C3%A9u_38.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Estadio_Santiago_Bernab%C3%A9u_38.jpg)Construction of the East side facade (4 April 2023). [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e9/Estadio_Santiago_Bernabeu_%2853988637843%29.jpg/330px-Estadio_Santiago_Bernabeu_%2853988637843%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Estadio_Santiago_Bernabeu_\(53988637843\).jpg)Interior and retractable roof in 2024. [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9e/Estadio_Santiago_Bernab%C3%A9u_40.jpg/330px-Estadio_Santiago_Bernab%C3%A9u_40.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Estadio_Santiago_Bernab%C3%A9u_40.jpg)The West facade of the stadium in 2026.
This proposal was announced at the Ordinary General Assembly on 12 September 2010,[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-34) and approved by the delegate members at the Extraordinary Assembly on 25 September 2011.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-35) To implement it, the [Madrid City Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madrid_City_Council "Madrid City Council") and the [Government of the Community of Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_the_Community_of_Madrid "Government of the Community of Madrid") approved a specific amendment to the General Urban Development Plan in 2012, allowing the club to increase the buildability of the stadium and modify its facade. The proposed plan included a new architectural envelope, roof covering for all seats, and the incorporation of bioclimatic systems with renewable energy, as well as the construction of two new public plazas, a hotel, and a large shopping centre on the side facing Paseo de la Castellana.
To carry out this proposal, an International Architecture Competition was held in 2012[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-36) in which four teams of world-renowned prestige participated: one formed by the studios of [Herzog & de Meuron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herzog_&_de_Meuron "Herzog & de Meuron") and [Rafael Moneo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafael_Moneo "Rafael Moneo"), another composed of [Foster and Partners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foster_and_Partners "Foster and Partners") and [Rafael de la Hoz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafael_de_La-Hoz_Castanys "Rafael de La-Hoz Castanys"), a third consisting of the teams of [Populous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Populous_\(architects\) "Populous \(architects\)") and [Estudio Lamela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estudio_Lamela "Estudio Lamela"), and a fourth formed by [GMP Architekten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerkan,_Marg_und_Partner "Gerkan, Marg und Partner"), L35, and Ribas & Ribas, whose proposal was announced as the winning project on 31 January 2014.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-38)
However, the project was halted in February 2015,[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-39) when the Superior Court of Justice of Madrid annulled the approval of the specific amendment to the General Urban Development Plan of Madrid, considering it contrary to the general interest and urban planning regulations. The court argued that the plan entailed a substantial alteration of land use and an unjustified free grant of urban development rights to Real Madrid. Faced with this situation, the club decided to modify the winning project to comply with current laws and reduce its urban impact. Thus, in 2016,[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-40) it presented a new project that eliminated the hotel and shopping center, raised the height of the stadium by only 12 meters (39 ft) for the construction of the roof, reaching a total height of 60 meters (200 ft), and eliminated the possibility of increasing the capacity.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-:2-7)
Finally, on 31 May 2017, the Madrid City Council approved the renovation by approving the "Special Plan for the Santiago Bernabéu Stadium".[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-41) After approving the replotting project, the sustainable mobility plan, and the urbanization project, the club awarded the renovation works to the construction company [FCC Construcciones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FCC_Group "FCC Group"), which finally began in June 2019.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-42)
For the financing of the works,[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-43) the Real Madrid board of directors approved a loan of 575 million euros on 12 April 2019, for 30 years with a fixed interest rate of 2.5%, including a 3-year grace period, resulting in an annual payment of 29.5 million euros starting from 30 July 2023. Additionally, on 7 December 2021, the financing was extended with an additional loan of 225 million euros for 27 years with a fixed interest rate of 1.53% and a grace period until 30 July 2024, with an annual payment of 10.5 million euros starting from that date. Finally, on 11 November 2023, a third loan[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-44) of 370 million euros for 30 years was requested to cover cost overruns due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_the_Community_of_Madrid "COVID-19 pandemic in the Community of Madrid") and [Russian invasion of Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine "Russian invasion of Ukraine"). Thus, the total financing amounts to 1.170 billion euros at an average interest rate of 3%, with an annual payment of 60 million euros over 30 years, which is less than half of the new expected annual profits after the completion of the works.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-45)

### Copa Libertadores
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Copa Libertadores")]
Main article: [2018 Copa Libertadores finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Copa_Libertadores_finals "2018 Copa Libertadores finals")
The two-legged 2018 [CONMEBOL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CONMEBOL "CONMEBOL") [Copa Libertadores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Libertadores "Copa Libertadores") final pitted [Argentine archrivals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supercl%C3%A1sico "Superclásico") of [Buenos Aires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buenos_Aires "Buenos Aires") in [Boca Juniors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boca_Juniors "Boca Juniors") and [River Plate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Club_Atl%C3%A9tico_River_Plate "Club Atlético River Plate") against each other in the final for the first time. The first leg was held at Boca Juniors' home pitch, [La Bombonera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Bombonera "La Bombonera"), on 11 November 2018, ending in a 2–2 draw with no [away goal rule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Away_goal_rule "Away goal rule") applied.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-Reglamento-52)
During the planned second leg on 24 November 2018 at [El Monumental](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estadio_Monumental_Antonio_Vespucio_Liberti "Estadio Monumental Antonio Vespucio Liberti"), the home stadium of River Plate, numerous River Plate fans threw glass bottles, bricks, dirts, stones, sands at the Boca Juniors team bus headed to the stadium, injuring numerous players as a result. CONMEBOL postponed and moved the second leg to Europe for 9 December 2018 on neutral ground at the Bernabéu for security and travel reasons.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-53)
Both sets of fans attended the match, and [Darío Benedetto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dar%C3%ADo_Benedetto "Darío Benedetto") opened the scoring for Boca before [Lucas Pratto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucas_Pratto "Lucas Pratto") equalised for River. With no further goals in normal time and no away goal rule, the match went to extra time. [Wilmar Barrios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilmar_Barrios "Wilmar Barrios") was sent off for a second yellow card in the 92nd minute, and [Juan Fernando Quintero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_Fernando_Quintero "Juan Fernando Quintero") then gave River the lead. Former Real Madrid midfielder [Fernando Gago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Gago "Fernando Gago") then went off injured, reducing Boca to 9 players having used all their substitutions, and [Gonzalo Martínez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pity_Mart%C3%ADnez "Pity Martínez") raced the length of the pitch for a clincher into an empty net as Boca sent goalkeeper [Esteban Andrada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esteban_Andrada "Esteban Andrada") forward in search of an equaliser with time running out. River Plate won 3–1 (5–3 on aggregate) to lift the trophy outside of South America for the first time. The second leg of the final was also the first Superclásico to be played outside South America.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-Reglamento-52)

### Cultural and social events
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: Cultural and social events")]
The stadium has played host to some significant political and religious events.
During [his pastoral visit to Spain in 1982](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_pastoral_visits_of_Pope_John_Paul_II#1980s "List of pastoral visits of Pope John Paul II"), [Pope John Paul II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_John_Paul_II "Pope John Paul II") addressed some 160,000 young individuals at the stadium.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-67)
In 2026, [Pope Leo XIV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV "Pope Leo XIV") will celebrate a [Mass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mass_in_the_Catholic_Church "Mass in the Catholic Church") at the stadium.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-68)
### Concerts
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: Concerts")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/50/Seguridad_Social_Bernab%C3%A9u.jpg/250px-Seguridad_Social_Bernab%C3%A9u.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Seguridad_Social_Bernab%C3%A9u.jpg)The Bernabéu hosting a concert on 26 April 2024
The stadium has hosted many touring musicians with dates in Madrid due to its expansive seating capacity and centralised location.
On 12 September 1983, [Julio Iglesias](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julio_Iglesias "Julio Iglesias") (who played as a [goalkeeper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goalkeeper_\(association_football\) "Goalkeeper \(association football\)") for [Real Madrid Castilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_Castilla "Real Madrid Castilla") in the late 1950s) performed for nearly 100,000 people at the stadium.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-69) On 21 September 1989, Iglesias gave a free concert to a crowd of 70,000 people at the stadium.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-70)
On 25 September 1986, [Frank Sinatra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Sinatra "Frank Sinatra") performed at the stadium, his only concert in the Spanish capital.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-71)
On 15 July 1987, [U2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U2 "U2") held their first concert in Spain at the stadium as part of their [Joshua Tree Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Joshua_Tree_Tour "The Joshua Tree Tour"), along with English bands [Big Audio Dynamite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Audio_Dynamite "Big Audio Dynamite"), [the Pretenders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Pretenders "The Pretenders"), and [UB40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UB40 "UB40") as the opening acts. Spanish journalist [Javier Menéndez Flores](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javier%20Menendez%20Flores "es:Javier Menendez Flores") believed that as many as 75,000 spectators may have been in attendance.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-72)
On 1 June 2002, the cast (16 contestants) of the reality [singing competition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_competition "Music competition") show _[Operación Triunfo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operaci%C3%B3n_Triunfo_\(Spanish_TV_series\) "Operación Triunfo \(Spanish TV series\)")_ performed a sold-out concert at the stadium as part of a 27-city Spanish tour. The concert aired on [La 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_1_\(Spanish_TV_channel\) "La 1 \(Spanish TV channel\)") to 5.14 million viewers, with a 39.5% share, becoming the most-watched concert in the country.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-concert-73)
[Bruce Springsteen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Springsteen "Bruce Springsteen") and the [E Street Band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E_Street_Band "E Street Band") performed at the stadium on three separate tours, making him the first artist to perform at the stadium on more than one occasion. The first date was during the [Magic Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic_Tour_\(Bruce_Springsteen\) "Magic Tour \(Bruce Springsteen\)") on 17 July 2008, where the band played to an audience of 53,783.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-concert-73)[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-74) Their second concert was part of the [Wrecking Ball World Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wrecking_Ball_World_Tour "Wrecking Ball World Tour") on 17 June 2012, with an audience of 54,639 people, the first time Springsteen and his band sold-out the stadium.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-75) Four years later, the band returned to the stadium on 21 May 2016 for [The River Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_River_Tour_\(2016\) "The River Tour \(2016\)"), performing to a sell-out crowd of 55,695.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-76)
The stadium was scheduled to host its first [music festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_festival "Music festival") on 30 June 2012, entitled _El Gol de la Vida_ ("the goal of life"), a [benefit concert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benefit_concert "Benefit concert") featuring Dominican musician [Juan Luis Guerra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_Luis_Guerra "Juan Luis Guerra") (as part of his [A Son de Guerra World Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Son_de_Guerra_World_Tour "A Son de Guerra World Tour")), [new flamenco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_flamenco "New flamenco") singer [Antonio Carmona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Carmona "Antonio Carmona"), Mexican singer [Marcela Gándara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcela_G%C3%A1ndara "Marcela Gándara"), and American [Christian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_music "Christian music") singer [Marcos Witt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcos_Witt "Marcos Witt").[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-77) However, the event was postponed and moved to the indoor arena, [Palacio de Deportes de la Comunidad de Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palacio_de_Deportes_de_la_Comunidad_de_Madrid "Palacio de Deportes de la Comunidad de Madrid") (the home of [Real Madrid Baloncesto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_Baloncesto "Real Madrid Baloncesto")) for unknown reasons, possibly due to weather concerns, scheduling conflicts or capacity issues.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-78)
On 25 June 2014, [the Rolling Stones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Rolling_Stones "The Rolling Stones") became the third international artist (and rock band) to headline a show at the stadium, when they brought their [14 On Fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/14_On_Fire "14 On Fire") tour to a sell-out crowd of 57,416 spectators. Local rock icon [Leiva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leiva_\(singer\) "Leiva \(singer\)") opened for the English band.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-79)
On 29 June 2018, the top 16 finalists of the [ninth series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operaci%C3%B3n_Triunfo_\(series_9\) "Operación Triunfo \(series 9\)") of _Operación Triunfo_ performed at the stadium in front of 60,000 people, as part of their Spanish tour. It was the second time, the first being in 2002, that the contestants of _Operación Triunfo_ brought their tour to the stadium.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-80)
[Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift") performed at the stadium on 29 and 30 May 2024 for her [Eras Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Eras_Tour "The Eras Tour"). Aside from being the first international artist to perform at the stadium in over a decade, Swift held the first concerts at the stadium following the completion of its renovation, which included updated technology to optimize the audience's experience at large-scale concerts, based on a comprehensive acoustic study.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-81) [Reem Abdalazem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reem_Abdalazem "Reem Abdalazem") of _[Diario AS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diario_AS "Diario AS")_ also noted that the concert's announcement marked "the first major event announcement for the newly constructed stadium."[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-82)
From 20–23 July 2024, [Colombian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombians "Colombians") singer [Karol G](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karol_G "Karol G") performed four shows at the stadium for her [Mañana Será Bonito World Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ma%C3%B1ana_Ser%C3%A1_Bonito_Tour "Mañana Será Bonito Tour"), making her the artist with the most performances at the stadium.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-:1-83) After announcing the first three shows from 20–22 June 2024, which sold-out in a matter of hours, the singer added a much-anticipated fourth show,[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-:1-83) marking the final dates of the European leg of her tour.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernab%C3%A9u_\(stadium\)#cite_note-:1-83) Approximately 200,000 fans, at least, were estimated to be attending the four-night spectacle. The 2024 concerts at the stadium marked Karol G's first performances given in Spain in at least five years, since the earlier days of her career when she performed at small venues and festivals around the country.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
[Luis Miguel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Miguel "Luis Miguel") performed in July 2024.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
